meta.purpose: THE DECISION REGISTER. One item per concept that is defined divergently across the programme's sources, each needing ONE canonical value plus an alias/supersession map. These are researcher rulings, not research: every item already carries the variants found and a recommendation, so each is a ratify-or-overrule call.
meta.why_it_exists: The programme's single most pervasive structural defect is the same concept defined 3-4 ways across the REF doc, the DB vocab tables, free-text SQL columns and synced patch copies — with divergent values (plan C.13). Rather than silently pick one, the config REFUSES to run on a contested rule and records the contest here until it is ruled on.
meta.how_it_binds: An item elsewhere whose value is contested carries status=RECONCILE and names its `recon.*` id (e.g. enum.role -> recon.role-enum). The loader will not run any study module depending on a RECONCILE rule. Resolving an item here is therefore what UNBLOCKS work — this file is the critical path, not a backlog.
meta.envelope: ⚠ THESE ITEMS DO NOT CARRY THE COMMON ENVELOPE. They have their own shape (below) and their own status vocabulary. A reconciliation is not a rule — it is a decision ABOUT a rule, so authority/intent/satisfaction/validation do not apply to it. See meta.open.envelope-exemption.

status_vocabulary.⚠ warning: `status` HERE IS NOT `status` ELSEWHERE. Every other config item's status is the rule lifecycle (LIVE / LEGACY / RECONCILE — see _manifest.json vocab.status). On a reconciliation item, `status` is the DECISION state and takes the values below. The two vocabularies share a field name and share no values. See meta.open.status-collision.

values.description: Not yet ruled. `decision` is null. Everything depending on this concept is blocked — no study module may run on it.

Ruled, but permanently live rather than closed: the decision holds AND the item stays open as the register of ongoing supersession edges (recon.live-vs-legacy is the case — the paradigm keeps moving, so its edge list keeps growing). Does not block.
Ruled and closed. `decision` holds the canonical value, `alias_map` maps the superseded variants onto it, and the dependent items flip RECONCILE -> LIVE. ⚠ NOT YET USED — no item has been ruled.

id.description: Stable code, `recon.*`. What RECONCILE items elsewhere point at.

concept.description: The thing being contested, named plainly — the question the ruling answers.

status.description: The DECISION state — not the rule lifecycle.

decision.description: THE RULING — the canonical value, once made. null while OPEN. This field, and only this field, is authority; a `recommended` or a working value in a dependent item's spec is not.

variants.description: The divergent definitions found, keyed by source. The evidence the ruling is made against, so the decision is taken on what the sources actually say rather than from memory.

recommended.description: The proposed canonical value, for the researcher to ratify or overrule. A recommendation carries no authority and is never read at runtime.

alias_map.description: Maps superseded variants onto the canonical value so existing data stays readable after the ruling. Feeds the loader's import mapping.

supersession_edges.description: For STANDING items: the record of what superseded what, and when. The programme's paradigm history.

sources.description: The documents the variants were read from — so any ruling can be re-checked against its sources.

note.description: What the ruling must settle beyond picking a value (e.g. recon.locus-vocab must also settle the Ps 1-25 blanket-convention data).

state.blocking: recon.mandatory-ledger blocks ledgers.json entirely. recon.role-enum, recon.resolution-vocab and recon.locus-vocab block their enums (and therefore any read that writes them). recon.ve-nr-master-list blocks the dimension set's boundary. recon.acceptance-sample blocks the definition of 'done'.
state.note: recon.acceptance-sample records a rule set verbally on 2026-07-14 (n=200/dimension, 0 errors = 95% confidence) that exists in no document — this register is currently its only written home.

open.issue: `status` carries two unrelated vocabularies depending on which file it appears in: rule lifecycle (LIVE/LEGACY/RECONCILE) everywhere else, decision state (OPEN/STANDING/RESOLVED) here.
open.consequence: One field name, two meanings, no way for a loader or a reader to tell which applies except by knowing the file. This is a textbook instance of the exact defect this register exists to eliminate — and it is in the register itself.
options: A: rename this field `decision_status`, leaving `status` to mean rule-lifecycle programme-wide
B: keep `status` and disambiguate by `kind` (loader dispatches on kind=reconciliation)
open.recommendation: A — cheap now (9 items, nothing loads yet), and it makes the field mean one thing everywhere. C is how the programme got here.

open.issue: Reconciliation items carry none of the common envelope (no governs/kind/version/authority/intent/satisfaction/validation), and `kind: reconciliation` is declared at the section level rather than per item.
open.consequence: The loader needs a special case for this section. Also `governs` is absent, so 'which processes are blocked by this open decision' cannot be queried — yet that is the most useful question this file could answer.
options: A: adopt the envelope — governs (what it blocks), authority (who ruled, when), version (rulings change)
B: keep exempt; it is a decision log, not a rulebook, and the envelope does not fit
open.recommendation: C — `governs` makes the blocking relationship queryable, and `authority` records who ruled and when, which a decision register must have. The rest of the envelope genuinely does not apply.

open.issue: There is no home for WHO ruled, WHEN, and ON WHAT BASIS. `decision` will hold a value with no record of its authority.
open.consequence: A ruling becomes indistinguishable from a default someone typed — and the recommendations in this file were written by an AI. Six months of this programme's failures trace to decided-vs-actual drift; a ruling with no provenance is that drift's seed.
open.recommendation: Add `decided_by` + `decided_date` + `rationale`, required whenever `decision` is non-null. Covered by meta.open.envelope-exemption option C (`authority`) if that is taken.
